Brexit and Donald Trump’s victories helped normalise political positions previously regarded as outside the governing mainstream, while successive economic and geopolitical crises have weakened confidence in established parties.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Driverless taxi services are rolling out fast across the world
stories.description: From Austin to London, the current robotaxi boom is raising hard questions about safety and jobs. We take a closer look in this edition of Tech 24.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Who could form a coalition with Germany's AfD after election victory?
stories.description: Germany's far-right AfD won a landslide victory in a key regional election Sunday in the ex-communist east, a result seen as a stinging rebuke for Chancellor Friedrich Merz, but looked set to miss out on an absolute majority to govern alone. The big question now is who, if anyone, will be willing to form a coalition with the party, says France 24's correspondent Nick Holdsworth.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: French wine yields drop to new historic low after searing summer heat
stories.description: French wine production is expected to suffer its worst harvest in some 70 years with the agriculture ministry on Monday forecasting a 6 percent drop in output after a summer of scorching temperatures, heatwaves and drought. France last week announced more than €1 billion in emergency support for farmers.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 'This might be the year': Mbappé embraces Ballon d'Or talk after World Cup exploits
stories.description: Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappé played up his chances of the winning the Ballon d'Or this year after scoring 10 goals at the recent World Cup to become the tournament's all-time leading scorer. Nominees for the prestigious award will be unveiled on Tuesday.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane overshoots runway in Miami
stories.description: At least five people died when an Amazon Prime Air cargo flight overran a runway and crashed while landing at Miami International ​Airport on Sunday, local ‌officials said.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Lebanon president calls for US help after deadly Israeli strikes
stories.description: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has urged Washington and the international community to help stop Israeli attacks, with strikes on the south of the country killing at least 11 people on Sunday despite a truce and a framework deal aimed at halting the violence.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Segregated schools and citizen ‘watch groups’: the AfD’s plans for Saxony-Anhalt
stories.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two. So who are the AfD, and what could it mean for voters in the state? Rachael Griffiths has more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Jubilation and pain': German far right marches to victory in key state election
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Monday, September 7: The far right marches to victory in a German state election: what does this mean for the future of Germany and Europe at large? Also: the Daily Telegraph publishes an exclusive interview with the sons of former Pakistani PM Imran Khan about his imprisonment conditions in Pakistan. Plus the US Open descends into chaos after influencers, weed and disruptions stir controversy.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Jamaica’s legal approach: Were forced transportation & African enslavement lawful under English law?
stories.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Jamaica’s Minister of Culture, Gender, Entertainment and Sport, Olivia Grange. According to Grange, the country’s reparations initiative attempts to shift the debate over British slavery from the terrain of political discretion to that of legal accountability. Was the capture, transportation and chattel enslavement of Africans in Jamaica ever lawful? Jamaica’s petition therefore asks King Charles III, in his capacity as King of Jamaica, to refer three questions to the Privy Council concerning English law, international law and Britain’s possible obligation to provide a reparatory remedy.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Far-right AfD wins crushing victory in German state election
stories.description: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting it within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two, though falling just short of an overall majority.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Why are tourists flocking to French pharmacies?
stories.description: After visiting the monuments and department stores, for some tourists in France, it’s off to the pharmacy. More and more foreign tourists are taking advantage of their stay to stock up on cosmetic products, sold in many pharmacies in France, which are known to be less expensive and very popular on social media.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: German startup carries out Europe's first commercial space launch
stories.description: German startup Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into orbit from Norway on Saturday night, marking the first ever such launch by a commercial entity from European soil. European firms are racing to make up ground in the lucrative launch industry, currently dominated by America's SpaceX.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: German startup notches Europe's first successful private orbital launch
stories.description: German startup Isar Aerospace becomes the first company to achieve a successful private orbital space launch. But first: Germany's far-right AfD party scores a big electoral victory, pushed along in part by the country's structural economic crisis and its fiscal policies.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Nepal holds a day of mourning as rescuers continue search for flood missing
stories.description: Grief-stricken Nepalis entered the traditional Hindu last day of mourning on Monday for the hundreds who died in the catastrophic flood along the country's border with China even as the government kept search operations going ​after four ‌miracle rescues in recent days.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany seeks to dismiss Nicaragua's Gaza genocide case at top UN court
stories.description: Germany is set to ask the International Court of Justice on Monday to dismiss a case accusing Berlin of "facilitating genocide" in Gaza by supporting Israel after the deadly October 7, 2023 attacks by Hamas militants. The details of the case, filed by Nicaragua in 2024, have not yet been made public.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Yemen govt forces, Houthi rebels battle for control of Red Sea gateway
stories.description: Military sources in Yemen say more than 140 combatants were killed in fighting between its government and Houthi rebels in the southwest of the country over the weekend. Days-long clashes have erupted in the country over the control of a gateway to the Red Sea, marking the deadliest fighting in the Arabian Peninsula country since a 2022 ceasefire between the two sides collapsed in July.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Signs of progress after US envoys Witkoff and Kushner hold talks in Ukraine?
stories.description: US peace envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff heralded new momentum in peace talks after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy in Kyiv on Sunday as the Trump administration renewed its push to end Russia's four-and-a-half-year war in Ukraine. But while there maybe some tentative signs that the proposals from the US team are more to Ukraine’s liking than those previously put forward, what Moscow thinks is still unclear, says France 24’s Oliver Farry.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes in Miami airport
stories.description: At least five people were killed when an Amazon cargo plane overshot a runway after it landed Sunday at Miami International Airport, officials said. Prime Air ⁠Flight 7598 overran the airport's diagonal runway shortly before 2 p.m. EDT (1800 GMT) and struck multiple vehicles on the ground, officials said during a news conference on ‌Sunday afternoon.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany: 'Hard to say' if AfD win the result of protest vote
stories.description: The Alternative for Germany (AfD) surged into first place in state elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, exit polls showed, putting a far-right party within reach of power at the state level for the first time since World War Two. However, France 24’s correspondent in Berlin, Nick Holdsworth, says it is “hard to say” if the victory is more the result of dissatisfaction with Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s governing conservatives, or an explicit endorsement of the AfD.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two far-right activists go on trial in Paris over 2022 killing of Argentine rugby star Aramburu
stories.description: Two-far activists go on trial in Paris on Monday over the shooting of Argentine rugby star Federico Martin Aramburu. Loik Le Priol and Romain Bouvier have been charged with murder and attempted murder respectively, and risk up to life in jail if they are found guilty.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: 🔴 Germany: Victory of far-right AfD in state election 'very worrying', says Polish FM
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ligue 1: Paris FC and Sinayoko beat Marseille and climb to 2nd
stories.description: Paris FC beat Olympique de Marseille 3–2 at the Vélodrome thanks to a hat-trick from Lassine Sinayoko. Paris FC sit second but OM remain stuck in 10th place in the table.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Wildfires, heatwaves threaten global air quality and health, UN warns
stories.description: Wildfires and heatwaves are threatening global efforts to improve air quality and protect human health, the World Meteorological Organisation said on Monday. The UN agency warned that increasingly severe fires are raising exposure to toxic PM2.5 pollution, even as regulations have reduced industrial and transport emissions in Europe and North America.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Middle East Live: Israel army orders evacuation of zone in south Lebanon ahead of strikes
stories.description: The Israeli army demanded early Monday that residents of Deir Zahrani in southern Lebanon leave a specific zone ahead of strikes against Iran-backed Hezbollah. Hezbollah's Al-Manar television channel later reported Israeli airstrikes on Deir Zahrani. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US envoys bring ‘more effective’ Ukraine peace proposals to Kyiv, official says
stories.description: US envoys brought new, “more effective” proposals to Kyiv aimed at ending the war with Russia, a senior Ukrainian presidential official said on Sunday. President Volodymyr Zelensky and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner described talks positively but announced no breakthrough, as Zelensky warned fighting could continue into winter.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: EU to boost Greenland investment amid Trump annexation claims
stories.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is expected to announce increased EU investment in Greenland on Monday, including in critical minerals, satellite communications and renewable energy. Her two-day visit signals support for Greenland and Denmark amid US President Donald Trump’s push for American control of the Arctic territory.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport, killing at least five
stories.description: At least five people were killed and five injured after an Amazon cargo plane overshot the runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday and crashed into several vehicles, officials said. Miami Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz said there was “no apparent threat to public safety” following the crash.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: "Ready to talk": German far-right celebrates victory
stories.description: “Everything is possible” is the election campaign slogan of the far-right Alternative for Germany, the leader in Saxony-Anhalt, where the polls have just closed. It talks of a seminal moment for the country. Ulrich Siegmund, who has been polling in pole position to become the state leader, knows he has history in his grasp.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴Germany’s far-right AfD landslide winner in key Saxony-Anhalt vote, early results suggest
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany’s far-right AfD landslide winner in key Saxony-Anhalt vote, early results suggest
stories.description: Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party headed towards a landslide victory in state ​elections in Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday, with 44.5 percent of the vote, early results showed.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Deauville Film Festival: What’s your favourite American film?
stories.description: The United States ranks second in the world in terms of the number of films produced. It produces between 500 and 700 films every year, which is just behind India. The Deauville Film Festival, with its stars, premieres and awards, aims to showcase the very best of what’s being made across the Atlantic. But on the other side of the screen, moviegoers also have their say. What’s your favourite American film? Is it one that shaped your childhood, or a recent discovery? Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca hit the streets of Deauville to ask that very question.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany: What could change in Saxony-Anhalt if the AfD wins?
stories.description: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election. Recent surveys place the AfD at just over 40%, followed by Merz's Christian Democrats (CDU) at 23%. If the AfD wins, "one of the main things they want to change is the education system. They say they want to reset education," our journalist Shirli Stibon explains.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Under-fire FIFA boss Infantino to seek re-election despite calls to resign
stories.description: FIFA President Gianni Infantino plans to seek his fourth and final term in next year’s election, despite the outrage sparked by his now-shelved plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. “Nothing has changed,” a spokesman for football’s governing body confirmed on Sunday, referring to an announcement Infantino made back in April.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The week in pictures: Nepal rescue operations, World Nomad Games and Russian strikes on Kyiv
stories.description: From the desperate search for workers trapped in the hydropower tunnels buried by the catastrophic flooding in Nepal to crowds of women mourning the victims of a US bombardment of a wedding in southern Iran, FRANCE 24 looks back at the week's most striking pictures.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany: AfD's Ulrich Siegmund eyes outright majority
stories.description: Under its 35-year-old lead ​candidate Ulrich Siegmund, the ‌AfD has polled above 40% for months and has a realistic shot at winning an absolute majority if several smaller parties fail ⁠to clear Germany's 5% hurdle to enter parliament.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Ukraine-Russia talks: What are the US objectives?
stories.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv on Sunday in their first official visit to Ukraine as part of a renewed push for peace, more than 4½ years after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. We discuss this topic with our guest, John E. Herbst, director of the Eurasia Center at the Atlantic Council.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Egyptian TV presenter Sarah Khalifa sentenced to death in drug case
stories.description: Sarah Khalifa, a well-known Egyptian TV presenter, has been sentenced to death for her involvement in a drug ring, state media reported over the weekend. Eleven others were also convicted in the case and handed a death sentence. Khalifa is best known for her program “Mission Impossible”.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: AI: The future of smart households?
stories.description: Could artificial intelligence soon be running our households? Beyond our smartphones, AI is now powering everything from fridges to lawnmowers. The International Household Appliances Fair in Berlin gives us a glimpse into what's next.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Germany: Why is the AfD so popular in Saxony-Anhalt?
stories.description: Voting began in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt on Sunday in a closely watched election that could see the Alternative for Germany (AfD) become the first far-right party to lead a state government since World War II. We discuss this with our guest, Hans Stark, professor of German studies at Sorbonne University.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Indonesia's Anak Krakatau eruption halts flights, schools, fishing
stories.description: An eruption of Indonesia's Mount Anak Krakatau caused six airports to suspend flight operations on Sunday, affecting hundreds of flights at Jakarta's main airport, after some school activities and fishing were halted.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Commemoration held for late Bosnian Serb war criminal Ratko Mladic
stories.description: A commemoration was held Saturday in Belgrade for war criminal Ratko Mladic two days ahead of his burial, attended by dozens of former military personnel, family members and officials.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany's far-right AfD clear frontrunner in eastern state vote
stories.description: German voters headed to the polls on Sunday for a key regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigrant, Moscow- and Trump-friendly AfD is expected to secure an easy majority. Our correspondent Nick Holdsworth tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ethan Hawke receives the Deauville Talent Award
stories.description: Known for starring in Dead Poets Society, the Before trilogy and Boyhood, Hollywood legend Ethan Hawke receives the #Deauville #Talent #Award in recognition of his career spanning nearly 40 years. He also plays the lead role in The Weight, screened at the Opening Ceremony of the 52nd Deauville #American #Film #Festival and due to be released in theaters on September 16. Our reporter Gaëlle Fonseca spoke to him on the red carpet.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll quits: "What we've seen is almost a factional clash"
stories.description: Amid the US conflict with Iran, Democrats and some Republicans are warning of a leadership void at the top of the US military. That's after the resignation this week of the Army's top civilian official, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, amid widespread reports of tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Our guest, Walter Ladwig, associate professor of international relations at King's College London, tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 🔴 Trump's envoys Witkoff and Kushner arrive in Kyiv after 'substantive' talks with Putin
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Iran claims strike on US ship in Strait of Hormuz as fighting escalates
stories.description: Iran said Sunday it struck an unmanned U.S. vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz, the latest salvo in a new flare-up of fighting between the two countries.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal floods: Search operations enter 12th day
stories.description: Nepali rescuers faced challenging conditions on Sunday as search operations following catastrophic floods entered their 12th day, buoyed by the extraordinary rescue of four survivors. The disaster has also affected infrastructure and roads. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany's far-right AfD clear frontrunner in eastern state vote
stories.description: German voters headed to the polls Sunday for a crucial regional election in the ex-communist east where the far-right, anti-immigration and Moscow-friendly AfD is expected to win easily.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli strikes kill four in Lebanon after alleged Hezbollah drone launch
stories.description: Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon Sunday killed four people, two of them women, the country's health ministry said. Israel's military said that the strikes were a response to an alleged Hezbollah drone launch targeting troops in the Israeli-occupied "security zone" in the country's south.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Eight airports in Indonesia suspend operations after volcanic eruption
stories.description: Eight airports in Indonesia, including Jakarta's main international airport, suspended operations Sunday after the erupting Anak Krakatoa volcano spewed clouds of ash across the archipelago. Geologists said that the latest series of eruptions does not have the potential to trigger a tsunami at this time.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: 'A bad sign': US envoys head to Kyiv after three-hour talks with Putin
stories.description: As US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner head to Kyiv following what the White House described as "substantive" talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, FRANCE 24 correspondent Gulliver Cragg talks about what he describes as a climate of scepticism in Ukraine that these latest negotiations could bring a long-awaited breakthrough.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Germany's far-right AfD eyes historic state victory in Saxony-Anhalt election
stories.description: Germany's anti-immigrant Alternative for Germany party is aiming to become the first far-right party to take power at a state level since World War II as voters in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt head to the polls Sunday. However, a failure to secure an absolute majority may see the politically isolated party struggle to form a government.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Witkoff: Putin’s Messenger?
stories.description: What did Steve Witkoff know about Russia when he was first sent to see President Putin in February last year?
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: The closely-watched Lindsay Clancy trial ends with one last dramatic moment
stories.description: The closely watched case of the Massachusetts mother who killed her three young children was on the verge of being declared a mistrial Friday — but there was still one more dramatic moment to come.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Wallace & Gromit' creators turn 50 with spook-tacular Shaun yarn
stories.description: Crochet hook in hand, the animator slightly raises the eyelid of a clay model sheep in a filmmaking technique as old as cinema, perfected over five decades by Aardman Animations.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UN approves resolution in support of map that shows Africa's true size
stories.description: The United Nations on ‌Friday voted for a shift away from the 16th-century Mercator global map towards one more accurately reflecting countries' true size, a resolution sponsored by African states to counter perceptions that the continent is peripheral.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Rain man’ to the rescue? France’s ex-president Hollande plots unlikely comeback
stories.description: Once so deeply unpopular he had to give up running for a second term in office, former French president François Hollande has slipped back into the conversation ahead of next year’s Élysée Palace race, hoping voters put off by squabbling candidates will come to see him as a safe – if unexciting – pair of hands after a decade of Emmanuel Macron’s ‘disruptive’ presidency.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Chinese national rescued from Nepal tunnel 10 days after flash flood
stories.description: A Chinese national was pulled alive from a tunnel in Nepal on Saturday, authorities said, 10 ‌days after a wall of ice, rock and mud tore through a Himalayan valley, killing more than 1,300 people.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: War in Ukraine: Putin, Zelensky order pause in strikes
stories.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin on Saturday ordered a 72-hour pause in strikes on Kyiv as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US envoys Witkoff, Kushner arrive in Moscow for talks on peace in Ukraine
stories.description: US special representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner landed in Moscow on Saturday for talks on how to end the ‌war in Ukraine, where they were met by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev. Our guest Jamie Smith-Maillet tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Culture of fear within US Defence Department: Slow leakage of dissent against the administration'
stories.description: Catherine Viette is pleased to welcome Dafydd Townley, Senior Teaching Fellow in International Security at the University of Portsmouth. He argues that the turmoil surrounding Pete Hegseth points to a problem much deeper than personnel disputes at the Pentagon: The removal and marginalization of experienced officials, the weakening of professional military education, and the prioritization of political loyalty risk changing the institutional culture through which the US military evaluates strategy and challenges political authority.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Paris hosts African Diaspora International Film Festival
stories.description: This weekend, Paris is hosting the 16th edition of FIFDA, the African Diaspora International Film Festival. From September 4 to 6, 15 films from 13 countries will be screened, spanning fiction and non-fiction, as well as feature-length and short films. The festival provides a space to explore how contemporary societies face and overcome wounds from the past, while giving a voice to members of African diasporas. Guest Lawrence Cole, co-executive producer of "Shadow of Greed", and Diarah N'Daw-Spech, FIFDA co-founder and co-director.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: Uber announces immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda
stories.description: Uber has announced its immediate withdrawal from Nigeria and Uganda. The decision comes amid a global restructuring, but mainly as Uber has lost significant ground to its competitors in both countries.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: UN experts urge Sudan-wide arms embargo
stories.description: A weapons embargo must be extended to the whole of Sudan, and it must be enforced. That is, in essence, the conclusion of a UN experts' report presented to the Human Rights Council. The report also points to the responsibility of foreign entities in a conflict that has now been raging for more than three years. Our correspondent Bastien Renouil tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal: Two more people rescued alive
stories.description: Rescuers in Nepal pulled out a Chinese man and a woman in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of missing people. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Witkoff and Kushner are in Moscow in a new push for peace between Russia and Ukraine
stories.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Saturday to try to revive a stalled push to end Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russian state news outlets reported. Our correspondent Gulliver Cragg tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France: Emmanuel Macron unveils new disability strategy
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron delivered the closing speech at the national conference on disability. It is an event the government holds every three years. It aims to set or guide policies. Macron made disability one of the priorities of his first five-year term. Since 2017, the government has implemented a number of measures to better integrate people with disabilities into society. According to official figures, between 5.7 and 18.2 million people aged five and older in France have a disability. We discuss this with our guest, Dr. Johny Daniel, associate professor at the School of Education at Durham University.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Presidential campaigning kicks off in France ahead of 2027 elections
stories.description: On April 18th and May 2nd next year - France will be voting to elect a new president to replace Emmanuel Macron. The country's latest opinion polls predict a victory for Marine le Pen of the Far-right National Rally. Although the election is still over seven months away, many potential candidates have already thrown their hats into the ring. But do any of them stand a chance of beating the far right? Our guest Eleanor Beardsley from National Public Radio answers that question.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two Nepal rescues revive hopes 10 days after flood
stories.description: Rescuers in Nepal pulled alive on Saturday a Chinese national from a tunnel and a local woman from her partially submerged home, as emergency response teams searched with renewed vigour for thousands missing since catastrophic flooding 10 days ago. Our correspondent Shahzaib Wahlah tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: DR Congo: Ebola burial teams race against time
stories.description: In eastern DR Congo, Ebola burial teams are racing against time as the outbreak continues to spread. They face a dangerous mission: safely burying victims while dealing with distrust and threats from local communities. The response is further complicated by the ongoing rebel conflict in the region.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US ambassador to Israel visits Palestinian town hit by West Bank settler violence
stories.description: US ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee on Saturday visited Turmus Ayya, a Palestinian town in the Israeli-occupied West Bank that has been repeatedly targeted by Israeli settler violence. Huckabee, a staunch supporter of Israel and its illegal settlements in the Palestinian territory, said that it was in the Israeli government's interests to take action against violent settlers.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Bangladesh measles toll nears grim 1,000-child mark
stories.description: Bangladesh's deadliest measles outbreak in decades is nearing the grim milestone of 1,000 child deaths, as a devastating epidemic sweeps through the country and crowded hospital wards fill with struggling babies.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'I don't know if I'm dreaming': Rebuilding lives after Nepal's devastating floods
stories.description: With thousands of people driven from their homes by a massive flash flood that swept entire villages away, FRANCE 24 visits a school in Nepal's remote Rasuwa district that has been converted to a temporary shelter for the dispossessed.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany: AfD eyes historic state election win
stories.description: In Saxony-Anhalt, AfD – Germany's far-right party – is polling at 40% or more of voting intentions, just days ahead of the regional election on 6 September 2026. If the AfD wins an absolute majority of seats, it could soon be in charge here. It would be the first time since 1945 that a far-right party has led a German region. To get there, the party is banking on the promise of a return to "the Germany of old", leaning on East German symbols such as Simson mopeds and retro aesthetics. It is a well-established strategy that draws on a gnawing sense of decline for decades and increasing distrust of traditional parties.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal: Temporary education centres help flood-displaced children
stories.description: Children displaced by flash floods in Nepal are attending a temporary education centre in Nuwakot, while aid organisations work to support devastated communities. The UN estimates that $158 million worth of buildings have been damaged, with Nepal warning that reconstruction could cost billions.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Monaco rally to edge winless PSG and reclaim top spot
stories.description: Monaco made it three wins on the trot and reclaimed the top spot by beating Paris Saint-Germain, who were playing their first home match of the season. Luis Enrique's men have now gone four matches without a win.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Trump sends envoys to Moscow, Kyiv with new plan to 'end war'
stories.description: US President Donald Trump said Friday he is sending envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv with a plan to end more than four years of war in Ukraine.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two senior Reform UK officials resign as Farage faces fresh foreign donations scandal
stories.description: Two senior officials from the hard-right Reform UK party stepped down Friday following a hidden-camera investigation that appeared to show them soliciting substantial foreign funding for party-commissioned opinion polls and a potential £500,000 donation from a US donor – banned under UK law.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Middle East live: Israeli strikes on south and east Lebanon kill three people
stories.description: Israeli strikes in southern and eastern Lebanon late on Friday killed at least three people and wounded 23 more despite a ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah, the Lebanese health ministry said. The ministry said in a statement that strikes hit five locations in the southern Tyre and Nabatieh regions and the Beqaa region in the east. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump sends envoys Witkoff and Kushner to Moscow and Kyiv with new plan to 'end the war'
stories.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are travelling to Moscow and Kyiv this weekend with what US President Donald Trump says is a new proposal to end the Russia-Ukraine war. Despite Trump's promises to resolve the conflict, Washington's efforts to broker a peace have so far come to nothing.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Uber withdraws from Nigeria
stories.description: In tonight's programme, a UN report says foreign fighters and support networks are fuelling Sudan’s war and worsening violence against civilians. Also, Uber is pulling out of Nigeria and Uganda, leaving thousands of drivers scrambling for new sources of income. And finally, we discuss the festival with co-director Diarah N’Daw-Spech and Laurence Cole, co-producer of the Nigerian film "Shadow of Greed".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: ‘Major potential breaches of British election law’: Inside Channel 4’s investigation into Reform UK
stories.description: Gavin Lee is pleased to welcome Peter Geoghegan, an award-winning investigative journalist. He's the editor of the Substack Democracy for Sale and the author of the best-selling book "Democracy for Sale". Geoghegan explains the significance of the Channel 4 investigation not simply over the conduct allegedly captured on camera, but in the broader question of how political influence is financed and made visible, or invisible, within British democracy.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: German power grid sabotage attack linked to ‘climate extremism’
stories.description: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt on Friday said the evidence in a recent spate of sabotage attacks on power grids across the country points to a militant climate activist.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: UN ditches Mercator map to adopt more accurate one reflecting Africa's true size
stories.description: The UN General Assembly on Friday voted to shift away from the 16th-century Mercator map, designed by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator, for a more accurate one reflecting the true size of continents. The resolution, spearheaded by several African countries and co-sponsored by France, was backed by 164 countries. The US voted against and six other states abstained.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany’s ‘Most Dangerous Man’: PR gift for the AfD?
stories.description: The Ukrainian capital was hit by Russia’s most intense wave of air attacks on Kyiv, reportedly in four years, with Reuters describing air raid sirens, drones, cruise and ballistic missiles exhausting Ukraine’s defence system, with 12 people killed and the Ukrainian foreign minister making a direct appeal to Western allies for more Patriot interceptor missiles.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israel's West Bank camp displacements could be crime against humanity, UN says
stories.description: The Israeli government's forced displacement of the entire populations of three West Bank refugee camps in January 2025 could amount to crimes against humanity, a UN report warned Friday. More than 33,000 Palestinians forced out of the Jenin, Nur Shams and Tulkarm camps have not been permitted to return home. Israel slammed the report for "spreading misinformation".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US midterms start with North Carolina distributing mail-voting ballots
stories.description: North Carolina on Friday became the first state authorised to begin sending out ballots, formally launching the 2026 US midterms as President Donald Trump’s administration fights to impose sweeping restrictions on the practice.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Italian opposition fragmented: No alternative leader, no other possible leader than Giorgia Meloni'
stories.description: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Political analyst Lorenzo Pregliasco, co-founder of polling agency YouTrend and adjunct professor at the University of Bologna. He argues that Giorgia Meloni’s unusual longevity in office is best understood not simply as a record of political strength, but as the product of a carefully calibrated governing strategy. Meloni has maintained stability partly by avoiding structural reforms disruptive enough to mobilize multiple constituencies against her at once. Her dominance within Fratelli d’Italia, the absence of a credible alternative leader, and a fragmented opposition have reinforced that advantage.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Germany: Hans-Thomas Tillschneider, the ideologist behind the AFD’s plans in Saxony-Anhalt
stories.description: The far-right German political party Alternative for Germany could win a historical victory in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt in key elections this Sunday. The party’s agenda is more radical than ever and inspired by the proposals of an influential ideologist in the region: Hans-Thomas Tillschneider.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Trump envoys Witkoff, Kushner to visit Russia and Ukraine in coming days
stories.description: US President Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to arrive in Kyiv for a first-time visit on Sunday, several sources reported. Witkoff and Kushner – Trump's son-in-law – have been involved in shuttle diplomacy between Russia and Ukraine, travelling to Moscow multiple times, and are expected to visit Kyiv this weekend. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: On the ground: Russian drone strikes Ukraine security service headquarters in Kyiv
stories.description: A Russian drone struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security services on Friday, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said, accusing Moscow of aiming directly at the SBU head's personal office. Zelensky said he had instructed the SBU to deliver an "appropriate, tangible response" to the strike, while Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiga described it as a "major escalation". FRANCE 24's Emmanuelle Chaze reports from Kyiv, Ukraine.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US judge declares mistrial in Lindsay Clancy child-killing case after jury deadlock
stories.description: A judge in Massachusetts on Friday declared a mistrial in the Lindsay Clancy murder court case after jurors were unable to reach a unanimous verdict on her criminal responsibility for killing her three young children. The case sparked a public debate over maternal mental health.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Ethan Hawke leads the charge at Deauville's 52nd American Film Festival
stories.description: The Normandy coast has become Hollywood-sur-mer once again, as the annual film festival welcomes talent from the United States. FRANCE 24's Genie Godula takes time out from hosting the opening ceremony in Deauville to bring us an overview of the features screening there.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France announces €1 billion aid for farmers after climate-hit summer
stories.description: France has recorded its hottest summer on record this year as the country battled heatwaves, drought and massive wildfires. The extreme weather has continued into September, with France's national weather service placing five departments on orange alert for several days. Temperatures are expected to reach 40°C in some areas. France's agriculture minister also announced a plan to unlock over 1 billion euros in aid to the agriculture sector, which has been severely affected by the extreme weather.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: 🔴 Russian drone ‘aimed directly’ at Ukraine security service HQ
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Strengthening Africa is an investment in Europe's future: EU Commissioner Jozef Sikela
stories.description: Are great-power politics back, at the expense of smaller countries? In an age of strongmen, is multilateralism in retreat? Not according to Jozef Sikela. The EU Commissioner in charge of International Partnerships insists that traditional multilateralism is alive and well, especially in the EU's approach to Africa and to the Arctic. We sat down with him for an interview at the European Commission in Brussels.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Trump administration unveils anti-immigration video games
stories.description: The #arcade #games are unveiled as the #Trump administration steps up its mass #arrest and #deportation programme of undocumented #immigrants. According to recent data, most of those arrested in July by #ICE have no #criminal record.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Himalayan hydropower buildout: Expert says risk management is key
stories.description: Following devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet, Access Asia takes a closer look at the fragile state of the Himalayan mountains. Dr Arun Bhakta Shrestha, an expert on the environment and risk management in the Himalayas, explains why it's so difficult to detect glacier movements in advance and says that the tragedy could serve as an opportunity to improve the way nations develop infrastructure in the resource-rich region.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: An inside look at Lucas Museum of Narrative Art in Los Angeles
stories.description: After years of delays and more than a billion dollars, the long-awaited Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is preparing to open its doors to the public in Los Angeles. The museum, founded by filmmaker George Lucas and his wife, businesswoman Mellody Hobson, will be a new home for visual storytelling spanning the Star Wars universe and beyond. FRANCE 24's correspondent Wassim Cornet reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nepal floods: Two workers pulled alive from tunnel after nine days
stories.description: Nepal's emergency crews have pulled two workers out of a hydropower tunnel where they had been trapped for nine days. The rescue comes more than a week after flash flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border killed more than 1,200 people. Both men have injuries to their hands and legs and have been airlifted to a hospital in Kathmandu for treatment.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Meloni celebrates milestone as Italy's longest-lasting government
stories.description: Italy's Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is celebrating a milestone: her hard-right government is now the longest-lasting in the country's post war history. In a country known for its political instability, it's a notable record. But considerable challenges remain for Italy's first female prime minister, ahead of elections next year. FRANCE 24's Italy correspondent Seema Gupta reports.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Struggling to make its voice heard: Can the EU forge a true foreign policy?
stories.description: "Who do I call if I want to speak to Europe?" The famous quote attributed to Henry Kissinger still resonates today. There is in fact a Mrs Europe on the world stage: Kaja Kallas, the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy. She is actually the sixth high representative. But ever since that post was created, rivalries between different centres of power have diluted the EU's ability to speak with one voice. We saw that recently with tensions over who should represent the EU in any potential talks with Russia.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli army has seized Lebanon's key Ali al-Taher ridge from Hezbollah
stories.description: Israel has seized the strategically placed Ali al-Taher ridge in southern Lebanon from Hezbollah fighters, Defence Minister Israel Katz said Friday. The Iran-aligned Shiite group did not confirm losing the highland, which sits around 10 kilometres from the border with Israel and was pummelled by Israeli strikes in recent weeks despite a ceasefire.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Strength of Meloni less linked to policy, more about her party's dominance within govt coalition
stories.description: William Hilderbrandt is pleased to welcome Dr. Giulia Sandri, Associate researcher at the Free University of Brussels. Meloni has benefited from something historically scarce in Italian politics: longevity. Four years of governmental stability have allowed her to accumulate diplomatic relationships, strengthening Italy’s position within Europe and giving Rome greater visibility internationally. Yet Sandri argues that this political success sits alongside a much less decisive domestic record. Improvements in employment and fiscal credibility coexist with weak growth, stagnant wages, declining purchasing power and persistent structural problems in healthcare, education, demographics and public administration.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Unearthing her story: The rise of women archaeologists
stories.description: In a show to kick off a new season, we explore the rise of women archaeologists – and how they are helping to transform our understanding of ancient societies. In the last 30 years, women have come to make up more than half of the profession. At the same time, advances in technology – from DNA analysis to carbon dating – are allowing archaeologists to build a far more accurate picture of the past. And sometimes, that means questioning assumptions that have existed for generations.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: What does acquittal in the Daphne Caruana Galizia case mean for journalists?
stories.description: This week, FRANCE 24's media show Scoop looks at the murder of anti-corruption journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia. Press freedom groups are furious after Maltese businessman Yorgen Fenech was acquitted of involvement. Caruana Galizia was an outspoken critic of the government and described as a "one-woman WikiLeaks". She was killed by a car bomb in 2017 and speculation followed that influential figures may have been involved. Our guest is the Times of Malta Editor-in-Chief, Herman Grech.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: 'Worst possible timing': Farage's Reform UK meets as new donation scandal hits
stories.description: British hard-right leader Nigel Farage's Reform UK party gathered for its annual conference on Friday engulfed by a fresh scandal. Just hours before Farage's address, two senior Reform officials resigned following an undercover investigation aired by Channel 4 News that alleged they had conspired to secure a foreign donation – barred under UK electoral law. The conference will also be addressed by Jordan Bardella, president of France's far-right National Rally party. FRANCE 24's Senior Reporter Clovis Casali tells us more.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Trump's White House releases deportation video games
stories.description: US President Donald Trump's White House on Thursday unveiled a website featuring classic arcade games – but with a "MAGA" twist, in which players can deport migrants and build a border wall. Rights groups swiftly criticised the release of the online games, which comes as the Trump administration steps up its mass arrest and deportation program for undocumented migrants.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Trump raises doubts over support for Britain in Falklands dispute with Argentina
stories.description: US President Donald Trump raised doubts about whether the United States would support Britain in another conflict over the Falkland Islands in an interview with a British broadcaster aired Thursday, injecting new tension into the long-standing dispute over the British-controlled archipelago also claimed by Argentina. Trump's comments came as his ideological ally, Argentine President Javier Milei, prepared to deliver a televised national address about what his government has described as diplomatic progress over the islands that lie about 480 kilometers off Argentina’s coast in the South Atlantic. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson-Bouyahe tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France announces €1 billion aid for farmers recovering from drought, heatwaves
stories.description: France on Friday allocated more than €1 billion in aid to support farmers recovering from droughts after a brutal, record-breaking summer. The allocation includes €520 million for rapid payments to ‌help farmers deal with weather damage and a €235 million recovery ​fund to buy seeds, plants and ​animal feed, Agriculture Minister Annie Genevard said.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: UK reasserts Falklands sovereignty amid Milei claim and Trump comments
stories.description: Britain insisted Friday that the Falkland Islands "are British" after Argentine President Javier Milei suggested the "winds of change" now favoured his country's claim to the archipelago, citing Washington's readiness to reconsider its neutrality in the dispute. The islands' fate returned to the headlines after US President Donald Trump threatened to wade into the dispute, while a British-Israeli oil project near the islands stoked anger in Argentina. FRANCE 24's London correspondent, Bénédicte Paviot, gives an inside look at Downing Street's reaction to these developments.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli minister unveils plan to remove Gaza's population over seven years
stories.description: Israel's far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir set out a plan on Thursday to remove Palestinians from the Gaza Strip and send them abroad. Speaking in the run-up to close-fought Israeli elections, he said the plan aimed to see the departure of 250,000 Palestinians from Gaza in the first year, followed by the rest of the roughly two million residents over the following six years. Forced displacement of civilians in occupied territory is considered a war crime under the Geneva Conventions.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: 'Moroccans are desperate: Years of political crackdown and lack of economic opportunities'
stories.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Aida Alami, New York Times World contributor. Drawing on her own field reporting at the Moroccan border, Alami challenges attempts to explain the mass crossing primarily through a theory of deliberate state orchestration. While acknowledging both Morocco’s history of leveraging migration in its relations with Spain and the possibility that security forces made tactical decisions on the day, Alami insists on distinguishing evidence from inference. Her reporting instead points toward an interaction between online misinformation, overwhelmed security forces, and a population already primed to migrate by political repression and limited economic opportunity.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Haute Couture, autumn-winter 2026/27: Make way for the independent labels
stories.description: Some couturiers get to modernise houses owned by luxury groups. Among them is Duran Lantink, who draws on Jean Paul Gaultier's ballet-costume era for his inspiration. Independent houses, by contrast, must create from scratch. Iris van Herpen turns to science. Rahul Mishra finds inspiration in the beauty of Hindu goddesses. Imane Ayissi pays tribute to his late mother. Finally, Kevin Germanier keeps celebrating the most desirable approach to recycling imaginable.
stories.subject: Science

stories.title: US state of Louisiana in battle over electoral map
stories.description: With just two months to go before the US midterm elections, the battle for votes is in full swing. Our reporter Fanny Allard has been to the state of Louisiana, where a redistricting row is playing out with far-reaching implications for racial equality.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Mass burial reveals hidden toll of Algeria’s deadly ‘Black Wednesday’ wildfires
stories.description: Wildfires ripped across northeastern Algeria in late August. Photos and videos showing the mass burial of several dozen people have raised questions about the real death toll of the fires as Algerian authorities haven’t shared new numbers since August 26. A number of Moroccan social media accounts have also been sharing disinformation about the fires.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Stability or fiasco? Giorgia Meloni becomes longest-serving Italian PM
stories.description: PRESS REVIEW – Friday, September 4: Italy's Giorgia Meloni becomes the longest-serving prime minister in Italy's postwar history. While she's celebrated by the rightwing press, the leftwing press say her leadership is a fiasco. Also, is Europe gearing up for a chaotic winter? Concern is mounting after the UN warned of a "supersized" El Niño phenomenon that could bring heavy rains and snow. Plus we look at tributes to Gloria Steinem, journalist and women's rights icon, who has died at 92.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two trapped workers rescued from mud-clogged tunnel 9 days after Nepal floods
stories.description: Nine days after catastrophic floods hit Nepal, hope emerges from the dark as two workers have been rescued from a collapsed tunnel. They are receiving treatment as emergency crews race to find more survivors. The floods killed more than 1,200 people and left over 5,000 missing. An estimated 115 people are still believed trapped in the tunnel.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Argentina's Milei escalates Falklands dispute in sovereignty push against Britain
stories.description: Argentine President Javier Milei said he would sanction oil companies drilling in the Falkland Islands, the British overseas territory claimed by Argentina, in a move which could escalate tensions with London. Milei's comments in a televised national ​address on Thursday came ‌days after US President Donald Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the ⁠remote archipelago in the South Atlantic.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: New fears of oil supply disruption as US-Iran hostilities resume
stories.description: Renewed hostilities between the United States and Iran have brought back fears of oil supply disruption. Prices are on track for their steepest weekly gain since mid-July, up 7.6%, as the US-Iran war enters its seventh month. Twenty-five percent of the world's oil supply comes through the Strait of Hormuz, which has been blocked since the beginning of the war. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Philip Turle gives more details.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: From forced labour to World Heritage: Sao Tome's colonial plantations
stories.description: Sao Tome and Principe's "Rocas" – colonial-era plantations – have been added to the UNESCO World Heritage List in July 2026, in recognition of their architecture and their fundamental importance to the country’s history. While the majority of them now lie derelict, they are attracting increasing interest from investors keen to develop the tourism potential of the history-steeped buildings.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: IOM ramps up emergency aid in Lake Chad as thousands flee Boko Haram
stories.description: More than 75,000 people have been newly displaced within Chad’s Lake Province following a resurgence in Boko Haram attacks in recent months. That is the latest figure from the International Organization for Migration, which is providing emergency assistance to meet their most immediate needs. Most of these tens of thousands of people have fled the islands of Lake Chad, seeking safety in towns and villages further away from the island areas. FRANCE 24's Harold Girard reports.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: #Nepal: Two flood survivors rescued from hydropower tunnel
stories.description: In a video posted to social media on September 4, the Nepali #army announced it had rescued two workers trapped in a hydropower tunnel. The rescue brings hope of reaching over a dozen others thought to be trapped inside the tunnel. Both men were flown to a hospital in #Kathmandu. The floods killed more than 1,200 people, and over 5,000 are still missing.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Nepal flood aftermath: Zip lines carry medicine as survivors relive the horror
stories.description: Eight days after disastrous floods in Nepal, as the death toll continues to rise, survivors are left struggling to access basic necessities. The shortages are adding to the hardships of those living in temporary shelters after having lost homes and belongings. While some are focusing on ensuring food and medicine reach devastated areas, many are now left grappling with the psychological trauma of the disaster.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Italy weighs the results as Giorgia Meloni’s government sets a longevity record
stories.description: In a country where governments are famously short-lived, the perceived success of Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni has often been attributed to her survival skills rather than her accomplishments. The record is likely to boost the prime minister's image as Italy, which has had almost 70 governments over the past 80 years, gears up for a national vote in 2027, analysts say. But recent events have complicated her path to re-election.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Nigerian police arrest four suspects over alleged organ harvesting
stories.description: In Nigeria, the police have arrested four suspects over alleged organ harvesting. Two of the suspects are medical doctors who are accused of carrying out the surgeries to harvest the kidneys. The victims are mainly vulnerable and uneducated youths whose financial desperation is exploited to illegally harvest their kidney for transplant to patients who are often wealthy, as FRANCE 24’s Sam Olukoya reports.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Why early warning signs of glacier collapse in Nepal were difficult to detect
stories.description: The glacier collapse that led to devastating flash floods across the Himalayan region of Nepal and its border with the Chinese autonomous region of Tibet on August 26 was preceded by early warning signs, experts say. But monitoring and emergency alert systems in the region are still insufficient to predict such disasters.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: USS Lincoln crew hits the streets of Thailand's Pattaya after nine-month deployment
stories.description: US sailors and Marines streamed into the Thai resort city of Pattaya Thursday after a record-breaking nine months at sea. Local police said there had so far been no major incidents connected to the 5,000-strong contingent of US service members, though two sailors were sent back to the ship after a drunken bar brawl.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: PSG look for their first Ligue 1 win against Monaco
stories.description: PSG have still not won a Ligue 1 match this season. After two games, the European champions have recorded two draws. The exact opposite is true of Monaco, who, with two wins from two games, are one of the teams in form at the start of the season. The two Ligue 1 heavyweights will meet on Friday in Paris.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Pragmatic international relations': Sánchez seeks to avoid 'further conflict with Rabat'
stories.description: Delano D'Souza is pleased to welcome Alana Moceri, International Relations Professor at IE School of Politics, Economics and Global Affairs. The migrant crossings at Ceuta have become both a domestic and international political lightning rod. At home, Pedro Sánchez faces opponents who can cast migration in existential terms, with Spain's far right amplifying the rhetoric of "invasion." Internationally, the crisis exposes the geopolitical leverage inherent in control of the border. Ceuta thus emerges as more than a migration crisis: the border becomes at once an instrument of geopolitical leverage, a weapon in Spain's domestic political contest, and a battleground for competing narratives and disinformation.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two trapped hydropower workers rescued from mud-clogged tunnel in Nepal
stories.description: Rescue teams on Friday pulled two hydropower workers free from a tunnel blocked by mud and debris during the massive flood that swept through Nepal in late August. Officials believe that hundreds of workers remain trapped in tunnels connected to hydropower projects throughout the remote Himalayan region.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Middle East live: South Korea prepares for military deployment in Strait of Hormuz
stories.description: South Korea is considering sending military assets to the Strait of Hormuz to support freedom of navigation, media reported Thursday, though Seoul denied it had decided on a deployment. Iran launched strikes on American military targets in the Gulf, in retaliation for an attack that killed four people at a wedding on Tuesday night. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: OpenAI begins rollout of GPT-6 with focus on cyber security safeguards
stories.description: OpenAI said Thursday it would begin rolling out GPT-6, its most powerful AI model yet, to select customers, touting stronger safety safeguards as concerns grow over the cybersecurity risks posed by increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Volkswagen to cut another 50,000 jobs to counter tariffs and Chinese competition
stories.description: Volkswagen announced Thursday that it will cut another 50,000 jobs worldwide under its biggest restructuring in the company's 89-year history, as the German carmaker faces pressure from US tariffs, overcapacity and fierce competition from Chinese rivals. The plan also sets out the future of four German plants.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Tunisia court upholds prison sentences of up to 45 years for opposition figures
stories.description: Tunisia's top court on Thursday upheld prison sentences of up to 45 years for opposition leaders, lawyers and businessmen convicted in a major conspiracy case, in a ruling opponents said further entrenches President Kais Saied's authoritarian rule.
stories.subject: Business

stories.title: Nvidia to buy Hugging Face for $12.93 billion in major AI expansion
stories.description: Nvidia said Thursday it will buy AI developer platform Hugging Face for $12.93 billion, its latest major investment to expand its influence in open-source artificial intelligence. The deal would bring Nvidia closer to developers and broaden its customer base as tech giants develop chips to reduce reliance on the company.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: '50% savvy political tactics, 50% extraordinarily good luck' - the formula to Meloni's success?
stories.description: Giorgia Meloni's hard-right government on Friday becomes the longest-lasting in Italy's postwar history -- a notable record that belies considerable challenges ahead of elections next year. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Nathalie Tocci, Director of the Istituto Affari Internazionali in Rome and Professor of Practice at the John Hopkins University SAIS. She says that Meloni's success comes down to "50 percent savvy political tactics and 50 percent extraordinarily good luck".
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Shady surgeons and Nigeria organ harvesting
stories.description: In tonight's edition, legal loopholes and gaps about specialised medicine may be driving Illegal organ harvesting in Nigeria. Also, South Sudan may be moving closer to delivering on elections scheduled for December. And on the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe, six colonial era plantation estates have just been added to the UNESCO World Heritage List.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: El Niño weather phenomenon set to deliver massive blow to global economy
stories.description: The UN warns El Niño is a "supersized" phenomenon that will hit the global economy. UK cider producers are feeling the impact of drought. Plus, Nvidia buys Hugging Face for $12.9 billion.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: No, UN chief Guterres did not call Francesca Albanese 'out of control'
stories.description: Pro-Israel lobby group UN Watch alleged that Secretary-General Antonio Guterres referred Francesca Albanese, the UN’s Special Rapporteur on Palestine, "out of control", saying he'd previously called her a "horrible woman." But Guterres named no one in his remarks. He said “many” independent rapporteurs were “totally out of control,” without singling out any individual. The UN has since said linking the comment specifically to Albanese is a “misreading” of his remarks. Vedika Bahl fact-checks.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Deadlocked jury in Lindsay Clancy's children murder trial deliberates for sixth day
stories.description: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial are deliberating for a sixth day in Plymouth, Massachusetts after twice saying they can’t agree whether the former labor and delivery nurse is criminally responsible for killing her three young children. FRANCE 24's Monte Francis explains.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: ‘Fight through darkness, water’: Nepal survivor recounts escape from flood-hit tunnel
stories.description: A Nepalese worker recounts his harrowing escape from a hydropower project tunnel after last week's devastating flood. Around 900 workers remain trapped in tunnels at six hydroelectric plants in Nepal as the number of missing in the Himalayan disaster rose to 5,624 on Thursday, according to Nepalese and Chinese authorities.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Anti-Christian murder in Syria? No indication he was killed because of his faith
stories.description: A Christian man by the name of Nader Boulos Tannous was murdered in Homs, Syria on August 15, 2026. After his death, Israel, Greece and Cyprus were quick to denounce what they called an anti-Christian act. Several days later however, authorities in Homs said the suspect had admitted killing Tannous as part of a personal dispute going back to 2012.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: WMO chief says El Nino could be strongest in four decades
stories.description: El Nino could be the strongest since records began four decades ago, the United Nations' climate agency warned Thursday, with the UN chief warning the world is in the "danger zone of extreme weather". The naturally-occurring weather phenomenon is set to become "very strong" in the months ahead and is near certain to persist through to February, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said. FRANCE 24's Journalist Carys Garland tells us more.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Two Palestinian teens killed in West Bank raid by Israeli settlers and army
stories.description: Two Palestinian teenagers ⁠were killed on ​Wednesday in an attack by Israeli settler militants and ​army troops on their village in the occupied West Bank, local officials and the Palestinian health ministry said, amid an uptick in violence ​by ‌Jewish settlers in the territory. The Israeli military said in a statement its forces had entered al-Mughayyir to ​provide security for police officers and an Israeli ‌civilian seeking to retrieve livestock.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: US energy firms dominate Venezuela deals worth billions
stories.description: US energy firms on Wednesday signed a raft of multi-billion-dollar deals with Venezuela, days after the South American country agreed to grant the United States control of a huge chunk of its vast oil reserves. President Donald Trump has talked up the agreement on Venezuela's oil reserves as the "biggest oil deal in world history." But the deals have raised major questions about Venezuela's sovereignty, as FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: France agriculture production sees economic hit from heatwaves
stories.description: France's recent heatwaves didn't just pose enormous health risks, they also hampered the economy. Authorities have estimated that the recent heat and drought caused production to plummet and expect wealth generated by the agricultural sector to decline by 8% over the course of the year. The knock-on effects will cost the French economy an estimated 0.1 percentage points of growth in 2026.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: US feminist icon and journalist Gloria Steinem dies aged 92
stories.description: The co-founder of Ms. Magazine and celebrated feminist icon Gloria Steinem has died at her home at the age of 92. An internationally recognised activist in the fight for women's equality, she spoke out for the legalisation of abortion, same-sex marriage, and equal pay. She began her journalism career in New York in the 1960s. Politically, she was an outspoken critic of Donald Trump, arguing that the US had taken many steps back when it came to women's rights. FRANCE 24's Journalist and host of "The 51%" tells us more.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Why Ukraine’s drained Kakhovka Dam is strategic for Russia
stories.description: Small groups of Russian soldiers have been inching forward through the vast, drained Kakhovka reservoir since they blew up the dam in June 2023. Russian forces are infiltrating this “no man’s land” for reconnaissance purposes rather than for a future military offensive, said a military expert.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Giorgia Meloni government becomes Italy's longest-lasting since World War II
stories.description: Italy's first female Prime Minister, Giorgia Meloni, has surpassed a longevity record set by the late Silvio Berlusconi. When she took office in 2022, many European allies viewed her with unease, given her party's neo-fascist roots. Yet she has governed pragmatically, working within EU institutions and even supporting Ukraine. Domestically, however, she has targeted same-sex parents and clamped down on press freedom.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: France-UK ties and humour celebrated as London receives Bayeux Tapestry
stories.description: French President Emmanuel #Macron is in #London on the occasion of the #Bayeux Tapestry's exhibition at the #BritishMuseum. The 1,000-year-old work of woven art recounts the Battle of #Hastings, in which William the Conqueror – #KingCharles's ancestor – led the Norman Conquest of #England. An opportunity for the French president, the British PM Andy #Burnham and British monarch to celebrate the strong ties between the two countries.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Driverless robotaxis hit the streets of London
stories.description: London is entering the era of autonomous vehicles: driverless cabs are now available through Uber and British tech firm Wayve in the capital. It marks a setback for Google's Waymo and Chinese giant Baidu, which have been eyeing Europe as a largely untapped market for autonomous vehicles. But for Wayve, it is its first mass-market rollout, and the company now plans to expand to Tokyo and 10 other cities with Uber.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: Murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia: Campaigner 'devastated' at tycoon's acquittal
stories.description: A campaigner who has worked on the case of murdered Maltese journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia since she was killed by a car bomb in 2017 has spoken of his devastation at the not guilty verdict.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Spanish PM Sanchez says no evidence Morocco orchestrated Ceuta border surge
stories.description: Spain has found no evidence to conclude that July's deadly border rush from Morocco into its enclave of Ceuta was orchestrated by Moroccan authorities, ​Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez ‌said on Thursday, countering allegations in a Spanish police report. Speaking in parliament, Sanchez responded to claims in ⁠the report that emerged this week suggesting the entry of over 70,000 people into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration but a planned effort to overwhelm border controls.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: Outrage mounts in Malta after acquittal over journalist's murder
stories.description: Hundreds of people demonstrated in the Maltese capital Valletta after a wealthy businessman was found not guilty of masterminding the murder of an investigative journalist. The verdict on Daphne Caruana Galizia's car-bomb killing in 2017 sparked outrage from Maltese civil society groups and international media freedom organisations. The opposition Nationalist Party, which organised the demonstration late on Wednesday, has said lawmakers should be called back from their summer break for a special session of the legislature to discuss the case.
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Beastie Boy Mike D releases his first solo LP 'Thank You'
stories.description: Mike D rose to fame in the 1980s as part of New York's Beastie Boys, a rap-rock trio who soon tired of poking fun at frat boy humour with hits like "Fight for Your Right (To Party!)" and" Girls". The band quickly moved on thanks to their passion for beat making, sampling and playing around in the studio, establishing themselves over three decades as credible genre-bending musicians.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: 'Glacier melt and sea level rise will continue: We cannot leave this to the next generation'
stories.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Inger Andersen, Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations and Executive Director of the United Nations Environment Programme. Her central argument is that decades of what she calls “carbon procrastination” have made exceeding 1.5°C unavoidable: the question is therefore no longer simply whether the world crosses 1.5°C, but by how much, for how long, and with what consequences for vulnerable societies and ecosystems. While mitigation remains essential, adaptation becomes equally important as sea-level rise and glacier loss, will continue even as emissions fall.
stories.subject: Climate

stories.title: Nepal Floods: Survivors hauled to safety with makeshift zip line
stories.description: Nepali authorities have erected a makeshift zip line to help stranded residents travel across the swollen waters of the Trishuli river after last week’s deadly flash floods swept away bridges, leaving them cut off from the outside world. Some were in need of urgent treatment, medicines, food and other essentials.
stories.subject: Health

stories.title: Please welcome the newest member to our team: The AI agent
stories.description: This week, we're looking look at efforts to incorporate artificial intelligence into the workplace. But not just your run-of-the-mill generative AI chatbot: we're focusing on actual AI agents. These are autonomous programs designed to take on tasks and work through a series of steps without the user having to specify every move. And they're moving into our everyday lives – helping people plan holidays, shop online and take care of other routine tasks.
stories.subject: Technology

stories.title: A 'Lille' bit of everything at Europe's biggest flea market
stories.description: Every year, millions of people flock to the French city of Lille on the first weekend of September for Europe's biggest flea market, the "Braderie de Lille". We dive into its rich history, the many terms for second-hand shopping in French, plus the delicious tradition that's now synonymous with this 34-hour event: mussels and fries!
stories.subject: Finance

stories.title: Tunisia water crisis deepens as temperatures approach 50°C
stories.description: In Tunisia, powerful heatwaves are driving power cuts and water shortage. While the country has been dealing with structural water scarcity and recurring drought for years, the current crisis is fuelling anger against the government, even as authorities attempt to coordinate water distribution efforts to quell the crisis.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France's Macron meets UK PM Burnham at Downing Street
stories.description: French President Emmanuel Macron met Britain’s new Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, for official talks at 10 Downing Street. The meeting came a day after the pair were joined by King Charles and Queen Camilla at the British Museum for a preview of the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition in London. Macron is the first EU leader to meet Burnham. Talks are expected to cover relations between Britain and the European Union, support for Ukraine, and migrant crossings in the English Channel.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Israeli attacks in West Bank at 'unprecedented' level, PNI leader Barghouti says
stories.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, the secretary general of the Palestinian National Initiative (PNI) party Mustafa Barghouti said the level of Israeli attacks on Palestinians in the West Bank had become "totally unprecedented". With tensions escalating, activists accuse settlers of operating with total impunity. "Their goal is clear: it is ethnic cleansing," Barghouti stated, calling Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's reaction to the attacks hypocritical.
stories.subject: Geopolitics

stories.title: Ceuta crisis: ‘No evidence Morocco behind border surge’
stories.description: There is no evidence Morocco was behind the mass influx of migrants that overwhelmed the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in July, Spanish PM Pedro Sanchez told lawmakers Thursday. Sanchez's comments followed a police report that emerged this week saying that the mass entry into Ceuta was not a spontaneous migration event but a planned and phased operation designed to overwhelm border controls.
stories.subject: World

stories.title: France recorded 'hottest summer ever' in 2026, environment minister says
